Class DecisionFigureText

java.lang.Object
network.ike.docs.koncept.DecisionFigureText
public final class DecisionFigureText extends Object
What a figure builder knows about text without a font engine: an estimate of a run's width from the average widths of a Helvetica-like sans face, in em per character, so the geometry a layout computes from label widths is the same on every machine and in every medium, and the figure's palette and number formats, which the live JavaFX surface shares.

Kept word for word in step with its twin in komet-claude-plugin, package network.ike.komet.claude.decision.render.

A stated number prints as the block wrote it, a computed one no wider than it earns, as shown(double, boolean, boolean) prints them.

    • quantity

      public static String quantity(double value, DecisionFigureText.Unit unit, String symbol)
      A quantity on a tornado's caption or threshold, with its unit: a share as a percentage, money after its symbol to the whole unit, anything else to three significant figures followed by its unit's name when it has one. A negative amount of money carries its sign before the symbol.

    • shown

      public static String shown(double value, boolean computed, boolean money)
      A measure's value as its chip shows it. A stated number prints as the block wrote it and no wider; a computed one is held to what its inputs can carry: money to the whole unit of its currency, a share or a quantity to three significant figures, since a product of two-figure assumptions never earns a fifth decimal.

      public static String tradeoff(String chosen, String other, double money, String moneyText, double health, String healthText, String priceText, String pricedText)
      What the choice at the root trades, as one sentence: how the chosen alternative stands against the next best in money and in health, and the price of a healthy year at which they tie, against the price the tree was read at.
      Parameters:
      money - how much more money the chosen costs, printed with its sign dropped; negative means less
      health - how much more healthy life the chosen keeps, printed with its sign dropped; negative means less

      A clause for one counted unit: who spares how many, per how many cases, and at what in money each, when the other side pays for it. "“scan” spares 3.3 ruptures per 1,000, at $590,000 each."; "“wear test” would spare 185,400 patients with an implant removed per 100, at $54 each."
